---
title: "Epicode: ATRX rescue in an ATRX-KO neuroblastoma line"
subtitle: "Bulk RNA-seq analysis"
author: "Arthur Dondi"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
params:
  # Point this at User.output_dir from your config, or pass it at render time.
  outdir: "/nobackup/lab_taschner-mandl/arthurdondi/projects/epicode"
  padj: 0.05
  lfc: 1.0
  # Order groups appear in every figure. Edit if you add conditions.
  condition_levels: !r c("TP53", "E6", "EmptyVector", "ATRX_FL", "ATRX_IFF")
  # The contrast the report leads with.
  headline_contrast: "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL"
  # ATRX_FL, ATRX_IFF, EGFP and mCherry are NOT listed here even though they
  # are constructs, not biology: with DesignQC.total_feature.substitute_as and
  # downstream_exclude_genes set (see config_epicode.yaml), the pipeline
  # itself already drops them before DESeq2 ever sees them, so they are never
  # in results.csv to begin with - filtering for them here would be dead code,
  # and worse, silently hide them again if that pipeline-level exclusion is
  # ever turned off instead of showing them as usual. ATRX itself still is a
  # row (it is now the pooled ATRX_Total: endogenous locus + both constructs),
  # still not pure biology, so it stays excluded from every
  # differential-expression figure and table below.
  exclude_genes: !r c("ATRX")
  # Labelled on the headline volcano.
  highlight_genes: !r c("HOXB2", "HOXB4", "HOXB6", "HOXB7", "IGF2BP1")
  # Every volcano additionally labels its N most significant genes (by
  # -log10(padj) x |log2FC|, the same ranking as the top-genes tables), the way
  # the pipeline's own volcano.pdf labels every significant gene. The report
  # caps it at a fixed N instead, since some contrasts have thousands of
  # significant genes and labelling all of them is unreadable at report scale.
  volcano_label_top: 12
  # Optional proteomics overlay for the headline ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL volcano.
  # Mirrors Proteomics: in config_epicode.yaml. Point proteomics_xlsx at "" (or
  # a path that does not exist) to skip the panel gracefully.
  proteomics_xlsx: "/nobackup/lab_taschner-mandl/arthurdondi/projects/epicode/251128_limmaResult_IP_MRa_051_LFQ_Experiment1_V3_filtered-KK.xlsx"
  proteomics_sheet: "limma result filtered"
  proteomics_gene_column: "Gene"
  proteomics_fdr_column: "_FDR"
  proteomics_logfc_column: "_LOG2FC"
  proteomics_fdr_threshold: 0.05
  proteomics_lfc_threshold: 1.0
  # DESeq2_to_proteomics comparison for the headline contrast (see the DIRECTION
  # note in config_epicode.yaml: proteomics columns read {numerator}_vs_{denominator},
  # the same convention as the DESeq2 contrast name).
  proteomics_comparison: "S1744_vs_S1011"
  # Section "ATRX interactors": internal neuroblastoma cohort, reprocessed by
  # Celine Prakash (full_omics_analysis.html, 2023-11-17). nb_expression is the
  # library-layout-corrected matrix (GeneID, gene_name, one column per
  # omics_id), plotted in "ATRX interactors". nb_counts is the same matrix
  # WITHOUT the layout correction, tested in "Patient cohort: ATRXdel, MYCNamp
  # and ATRXwtMYCNwt" with the layout in the model. nb_metadata is an Excel
  # sheet (omics_id, sample_id, classification, library_layout); tissue,
  # patient and timepoint are read from omics_id, TISSUE_PATIENT_TIMEPOINT_N.
  # All three are patient data: they stay on the cluster and are never
  # committed. Point nb_metadata at "" to skip both patient sections.
  nb_expression: "/nobackup/lab_taschner-mandl/arthurdondi/data/reanalysis.NB.bulkRNA/full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts_liblayout_corrected.csv"
  nb_counts: "/nobackup/lab_taschner-mandl/arthurdondi/data/reanalysis.NB.bulkRNA/full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts.csv"
  nb_metadata: "/nobackup/lab_taschner-mandl/arthurdondi/data/reanalysis.NB.bulkRNA/metadata_table_wStage.xlsx"
  nb_metadata_sheet: 1
  # omics_id prefixes that differ between the sample sheet and the expression
  # matrices: sheet prefix = matrix prefix. The sheet calls the controls
  # control_060_REL where the matrices have BMn_060_REL.
  nb_id_prefix_alias: !r c(control = "BMn")
  # Interactor list; "" = analysis/atrx_interactors/atrx_interactors.tsv in
  # this repository.
  atrx_interactors: ""
  # Gene-set size limits for the patient GSEA, as GSEA.min_size / max_size in
  # config_epicode.yaml.
  gsea_min_size: 9
  gsea_max_size: 500
  # Every plot as its own PDF in <export_dir>/figures/<section>/, every table
  # as a CSV in <export_dir>/tables/<section>/. "" = <outdir>/report, next to
  # the HTML the Snakemake rule writes. Both folders are emptied at each render.
  export: TRUE
  export_dir: ""
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    toc_depth: 3
    number_sections: true
    self_contained: true
    theme: flatly
    fig_width: 9
    fig_height: 5
    df_print: kable
    # Every chunk's code is included but folded behind a "Show" toggle, so the
    # report reads as figures and tables by default while staying fully
    # reproducible one click away. Requires echo = TRUE in the setup chunk below
    # - code_folding only folds code that would otherwise be printed.
    code_folding: hide
  pdf_document:
    toc: true
    number_sections: true
    fig_width: 8
    fig_height: 4.5
---

<!--
HOW TO RENDER
  Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("report/analysis_report.Rmd",
              params = list(outdir = "/path/to/output_dir"),
              output_file = "analysis_report.html")'

  Swap output_format = "pdf_document" for PDF (needs LaTeX).

HOW THIS WORKS
  Every figure is rebuilt here from the CSV files the pipeline already writes,
  rather than embedding the PDFs. That keeps the styling consistent, makes the
  HTML self-contained, and means you can edit any plot in this file.

  Every section degrades gracefully: if an output is missing the section says so
  and the report still renders. So you can run it before the pipeline finishes.

  Text in > blockquotes is placeholder interpretation - rewrite it.

  Every plot is also saved as a PDF under <export_dir>/figures/<section>/ and
  every table as a CSV under <export_dir>/tables/<section>/ (params$export).
-->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# echo = TRUE + code_folding: hide (in the YAML header) is the "Show" toggle
# per chunk - code is present in the HTML but folded away by default.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      dpi = 150, fig.align = "center")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(knitr)
})

OUT <- params$outdir
LEV <- params$condition_levels

# ── Per-plot PDFs and per-table CSVs ─────────────────────────────────────────
# <export_dir>/figures/<NN_section>/ and <export_dir>/tables/<NN_section>/, the
# section folders numbered and named after the report's top-level headings.
# Plots knitr draws are saved by a second graphics device (PDF next to the PNG
# it embeds) and copied over by the last chunk; plots drawn through
# show_plot() and tables printed through kable() are written straight away.
# Files are named <chunk label>-<n> unless export_as() names them.
EXPORT <- isTRUE(params$export)
EXPORT_DIR <- if (nzchar(params$export_dir)) params$export_dir else file.path(OUT, "report")
FIG_DIR <- file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "figures")
TAB_DIR <- file.path(EXPORT_DIR, "tables")
# cairo_pdf embeds the non-ASCII characters (★, ≤, —) the plots use; pdf() would not.
PDF_DEV <- if (isTRUE(capabilities("cairo"))) "cairo_pdf" else "pdf"
if (EXPORT) {
  unlink(c(FIG_DIR, TAB_DIR), recursive = TRUE)
  dir.create(FIG_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(TAB_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = c("png", PDF_DEV))
}

# Chunk label -> section folder, read from this file's own top-level headings
# (number_sections numbers them in the same order). Lines inside code chunks
# are skipped: an R comment also starts with "# ".
SECTION_OF <- local({
  slug <- function(x) gsub("^_|_$", "", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x))
  lines <- readLines(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  in_chunk <- FALSE; sec <- "00_setup"; i <- 0; map <- character()
  for (l in lines) {
    if (grepl("^\\s*```", l)) {
      lab <- regmatches(l, regexec("^\\s*```\\{r[ ,]+([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\\s*[,}]", l))[[1]]
      if (!in_chunk && length(lab) == 2) map[lab[2]] <- sec
      in_chunk <- !in_chunk
      next
    }
    if (!in_chunk && grepl("^# ", l)) {
      i <- i + 1
      sec <- sprintf("%02d_%s", i, slug(sub("^# +", "", l)))
    }
  }
  map
})
cur_section <- function(label = knitr::opts_current$get("label")) {
  s <- if (is.null(label)) NA else SECTION_OF[label]
  if (is.na(s)) "unsorted" else unname(s)
}

# One-shot names for the next exported plot and/or table, e.g.
# export_as("all/ATRX_DEL_vs_MNA_volcano"); "/" makes subfolders.
.export <- new.env()
.export$n <- list()
export_as <- function(plot = NULL, table = NULL) {
  .export$plot <- plot
  .export$table <- table
}
export_path <- function(root, kind, ext, name = NULL) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) label <- "chunk"
  if (is.null(name)) {
    name <- .export[[kind]]
    .export[[kind]] <- NULL
  }
  if (is.null(name)) {
    key <- paste(kind, label)
    .export$n[[key]] <- (if (is.null(.export$n[[key]])) 0 else .export$n[[key]]) + 1
    # "-fig" keeps these apart from knitr's own <label>-<n>.pdf in the same chunk.
    name <- sprintf("%s-%s%d", label, if (kind == "plot") "fig" else "", .export$n[[key]])
  }
  f <- file.path(root, cur_section(label), paste0(name, ext))
  dir.create(dirname(f), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  f
}
export_plot <- function(p, width, height, name = NULL) {
  if (!EXPORT) return(invisible())
  try(ggsave(export_path(FIG_DIR, "plot", ".pdf", name), p, width = width,
             height = height, device = get(PDF_DEV)), silent = TRUE)
}
# HTML markup (bold totals, line breaks) is stripped from the CSV, and fmt_p()'s
# non-breaking hyphens turned back into plain minus signs.
export_table <- function(x, name = NULL) {
  if (!EXPORT) return(invisible())
  d <- as.data.frame(x, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (j in seq_along(d)) {
    if (is.list(d[[j]])) d[[j]] <- vapply(d[[j]], paste, "", collapse = ";")
    if (is.character(d[[j]]) || is.factor(d[[j]]))
      d[[j]] <- gsub("\u2011", "-", gsub("<[^>]+>", "", as.character(d[[j]])), fixed = TRUE)
  }
  rn <- !identical(rownames(d), as.character(seq_len(nrow(d))))
  try(write.csv(d, export_path(TAB_DIR, "table", ".csv", name), row.names = rn),
      silent = TRUE)
}
# Every table in the report goes through kable(), so this wrapper exports each
# one as it is printed.
kable <- function(x, ...) {
  export_table(x)
  knitr::kable(x, ...)
}

# Condition palette from the lab colour sheet (20261021_Colors.pdf): one fixed
# colour per line, keyed by name so editing condition_levels cannot reshuffle
# them (1760 = EmptyVector, 1011 = ATRX_FL, 1744 = ATRX_IFF, see
# config_epicode.yaml). Conditions not on the sheet fall back to grey. Keep in
# sync with condition_colours in analysis/atrx_interactors/boxplot_helpers.R.
COND_COLOURS <- c(TP53 = "#ABAB50", E6 = "#46184E", EmptyVector = "#D16530",
                  ATRX_FL = "#19468C", ATRX_IFF = "#B72656")
PAL <- setNames(ifelse(LEV %in% names(COND_COLOURS), COND_COLOURS[LEV], "grey60"), LEV)

# Volcano colours from the same sheet: significant genes green on the left
# (log2FC < 0), pink on the right (log2FC > 0). Non-significant genes are a
# light grey, not grey70: grey70 is indistinguishable from the pink under
# protanopia. The sheet's spare blue marks highlighted genes and proteomics hits.
VOLC_COL <- c(down = "#4C5021", up = "#E5A6B7", ns = "#E6E6E6")
HL_COL   <- "#6D8AB6"

# Enrichment plots (GSEA, GO, over-representation): padj on a single-hue blue
# ramp, dark where padj is lowest. Neither the old red ramp nor viridis, which
# the proteomics analysis uses, so transcriptomic and proteomic enrichment
# panels never share a colour scale. log10 scale from `floor` (anything lower,
# including 0, gets the darkest colour) to the cutoff.
scale_colour_padj <- function(cut = params$padj, name = "padj", floor = 1e-10) {
  # Every 2 decades up to 1e-4; 1e-2 would sit on top of the 0.05 cutoff.
  brk <- c(floor, 10^-(seq(-log10(floor) - 2, 4, by = -2)), cut)
  brk <- sort(unique(brk[brk >= floor & brk <= cut]))
  scale_colour_gradient(
    low = "#0d366b", high = "#86b6ef", trans = "log10", limits = c(floor, cut),
    breaks = brk,
    labels = ifelse(brk == floor, paste("\u2264", format(floor)), vapply(brk, format, "")),
    oob = function(x, range) scales::squish(x, range, only.finite = FALSE), name = name)
}

# Whole-number size legend (counts of genes): about 3 pretty breaks, rounded.
int_breaks <- function(lim) {
  b <- unique(round(pretty(lim, n = 3)))
  b[b >= lim[1] & b <= lim[2]]
}

# Draw a plot as an image of the given size (inches). scroll = TRUE puts it in
# a horizontally scrollable box at full width, so long pathway names do not
# squeeze the panel.
show_plot <- function(p, width, height, scroll = FALSE, name = NULL) {
  if (!knitr::is_html_output()) return(print(p))  # knitr's devices export it
  export_plot(p, width, height, name)
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ggsave(f, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  # Tag built with paste0, not a sprintf template: rmarkdown scans the whole
  # page, folded source code included, for img src attributes and warns on a
  # literal "%s" there.
  img <- paste0('<img src="', knitr::image_uri(f), '" style="width: ', round(width * 96),
                'px; max-width: ', if (scroll) "none" else "100%", ';">')
  cat("\n", if (scroll) sprintf('<div style="overflow-x: auto;">%s</div>', img) else img, "\n\n")
}

# Enrichment dot plot sized to its labels and number of rows.
# The dot panel always gets panel_width inches: everything around it (pathway
# names, facet strips, legends) is measured on the built plot and added on top,
# so long names widen the image, and the scroll box, instead of squeezing the
# panel. 8.4 in (~810 px) fits the report column; only wider plots scroll. At
# least 4 in tall so the legends fit; titles start at the left edge, not over
# the panel, which long labels push far right. `labels` is kept for callers
# but no longer used: the measurement covers it.
show_enrich <- function(p, labels, n_rows, panel_width = 3.5, name = NULL) {
  p <- p + theme(plot.title.position = "plot")
  # Text widths need a device: a null PDF, closed straight away, then the
  # device knitr draws on made current again (dev.off() would otherwise pick
  # whichever device comes next).
  prev <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  grDevices::pdf(NULL)
  dev <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  g <- ggplotGrob(p)
  panel_cols <- unique(unlist(g$layout[grepl("^panel", g$layout$name), c("l", "r")]))
  around <- grid::convertWidth(sum(g$widths[-panel_cols]), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
  grDevices::dev.off(dev)
  if (prev > 1) grDevices::dev.set(prev)
  show_plot(p, width = max(8.4, around + panel_width),
            height = max(4, 1.8 + 0.26 * n_rows), scroll = TRUE, name = name)
}

# A table in a scrollable box (both directions), under the plot it lists.
scroll_table <- function(d, max_height = 300) {
  cat(sprintf('<div style="max-height: %dpx; overflow: auto; margin-bottom: 1.5em;">\n',
              max_height))
  print(kable(d, format = "html", row.names = FALSE,
              # "enrich": see the <style> block after the setup chunk.
              table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed enrich" style="font-size: 85%;"'))
  cat("\n</div>\n\n")
}

# p-values as text (2 significant digits): kable would otherwise reformat a
# numeric column and print tiny values as 0.00. Non-breaking hyphen so
# "9.9e-24" does not wrap in a narrow column.
fmt_p <- function(x) gsub("-", "\u2011", formatC(x, format = "g", digits = 2), fixed = TRUE)

# Gene lists as written by fgsea (";") or shared_genes.R ("/"), comma-separated.
genes_list <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) "" else gsub("[;/]", ", ", x)

# The table under a GSEA dot plot: the plotted pathways, top to bottom.
gsea_table <- function(df) {
  df <- df[order(-df$NES), , drop = FALSE]
  scroll_table(data.frame(pathway = as.character(df$pathway), NES = round(df$NES, 2),
                          padj = fmt_p(df$padj), `set size` = df$size,
                          `leading-edge genes` = genes_list(df$leadingEdge),
                          check.names = FALSE))
}

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
theme_update(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
             plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
             plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey30", size = 9))

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Read a pipeline output, or return NULL and leave a visible note in the report.
grab <- function(...) {
  f <- file.path(OUT, ...)
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}
missing_note <- function(...) {
  cat("\n> **Not available.** `", file.path(...), "` was not found. ",
      "Run that part of the pipeline and re-render.\n\n", sep = "")
}
cond_factor <- function(x) factor(x, levels = LEV[LEV %in% unique(x)])

# Long-format helper for the wide per-gene tables (gene_id + one column per sample).
gene_long <- function(df, meta) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
  df %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene_id, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
    left_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(condition = cond_factor(condition),
           sample = factor(sample, levels = meta$sample))
}

# Sample sheet, used to colour everything by condition.
qc <- grab("design_qc", "design_qc_summary.csv")
meta <- if (!is.null(qc)) {
  qc %>% select(sample, condition) %>%
    arrange(match(condition, LEV)) %>%
    mutate(condition = cond_factor(condition))
} else NULL

# DESeq results with the vector/transgene features dropped. They are guaranteed
# to be the most significant genes in any contrast that crosses a construct
# boundary, and they say nothing about the cells' biology.
de_results <- function(...) {
  r <- grab(...)
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  n0 <- nrow(r)
  r  <- r[!tolower(r$gene_id) %in% tolower(params$exclude_genes), , drop = FALSE]
  attr(r, "n_dropped") <- n0 - nrow(r)
  r
}

# Volcano dots, shared by volcano() and volcano_with_proteomic(): the
# non-significant genes first, then the significant ones on top, coloured by
# side (VOLC_COL: green left, pink right). res needs a logical `sig` column.
volcano_dots <- function(res) {
  list(
    geom_point(data = filter(res, !sig), colour = VOLC_COL[["ns"]], size = 0.8),
    geom_point(aes(colour = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "up", "down")),
               data = filter(res, sig), size = 1, alpha = 0.9),
    scale_colour_manual(values = VOLC_COL, guide = "none"))
}

volcano <- function(res, title, num, den, highlight = NULL,
                    label_top = params$volcano_label_top) {
  res <- res %>% filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    mutate(sig = padj < params$padj & abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc)
  n <- c(up = sum(res$sig & res$log2FoldChange > 0),
         down = sum(res$sig & res$log2FoldChange < 0))
  p <- ggplot(res, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj))) +
    volcano_dots(res) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-params$lfc, params$lfc), linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(params$padj), linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      # Spell the direction out on both axes: "up in X" is ambiguous unless the
      # reader already knows which group is the numerator.
      subtitle = sprintf(
        paste0("%s significant (padj < %s, |log2FC| >= %s)\n",
               "RIGHT, log2FC > 0: %s genes HIGHER in %s   |   ",
               "LEFT, log2FC < 0: %s genes HIGHER in %s"),
        format(sum(res$sig), big.mark = ","), params$padj, params$lfc,
        format(n["up"], big.mark = ","), num,
        format(n["down"], big.mark = ","), den),
      x = sprintf("log2FC  (%s / %s)   \u2014   positive = higher in %s", num, den, num),
      y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p")) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(lineheight = 1.2))
  # Label the most significant genes, ranked the same way as top_genes():
  # -log10(padj) x |log2FC|, so the labelled genes match the accompanying table.
  # The pipeline's own volcano.pdf labels every significant gene; capped here
  # because report-scale figures become unreadable once a contrast has more
  # than a few dozen significant genes (E6_vs_TP53 has thousands).
  hl_lower <- if (is.null(highlight)) character(0) else tolower(highlight)
  if (label_top > 0) {
    lbl <- res %>% filter(sig, !tolower(gene_id) %in% hl_lower) %>%
      mutate(score = -log10(padj) * abs(log2FoldChange)) %>%
      slice_max(score, n = label_top, with_ties = FALSE)
    if (nrow(lbl)) {
      p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = lbl, aes(label = gene_id), colour = "grey20", size = 2.4,
        max.overlaps = 30, segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey50",
        show.legend = FALSE)
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(highlight)) {
    h <- res %>% filter(tolower(gene_id) %in% hl_lower)
    if (nrow(h)) {
      # Drawn after the general labels so the highlighted genes and their
      # labels sit on top rather than being obscured by them.
      # Blue point, dark label: green now means "significant, right side".
      p <- p +
        geom_point(data = h, shape = 21, fill = HL_COL, colour = "grey15",
                   size = 2.6, stroke = 0.4) +
        ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
          data = h, aes(label = gene_id), colour = "grey10", fontface = "bold",
          size = 3.1, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.6,
          segment.colour = HL_COL, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE)
    }
    miss <- setdiff(hl_lower, tolower(res$gene_id))
    if (length(miss)) message("highlight not found: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
  }
  p
}

# Ranking by padj alone floats high-count genes with tiny fold-changes to the
# top. This ranks significant genes by -log10(padj) * |log2FC| so both matter,
# and reports the two directions separately so one cannot crowd out the other.
top_genes <- function(res, n = 10) {
  res %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < params$padj,
                 abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc) %>%
    mutate(direction = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "up", "down"),
           score = -log10(padj) * abs(log2FoldChange)) %>%
    group_by(direction) %>% slice_max(score, n = n) %>% ungroup() %>%
    arrange(direction, desc(score)) %>%
    transmute(gene_id, direction, baseMean = round(baseMean),
              log2FC = round(log2FoldChange, 2), padj = signif(padj, 3),
              score = round(score, 1))
}

de_counts <- function(res) {
  r <- res %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < params$padj,
                      abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc)
  c(up = sum(r$log2FoldChange > 0), down = sum(r$log2FoldChange < 0))
}

# Proteomics-significant genes for one comparison, wide-format limma Excel.
# Mirrors workflow/scripts/deseq2_proteomic.R. Returns NULL (and lets the
# caller show missing_note()) if the file, sheet or columns are not there.
load_proteomics_sig <- function() {
  if (!nchar(params$proteomics_xlsx) || !file.exists(params$proteomics_xlsx)) return(NULL)
  logfc_col <- paste0(params$proteomics_comparison, params$proteomics_logfc_column)
  fdr_col   <- paste0(params$proteomics_comparison, params$proteomics_fdr_column)
  tbl <- tryCatch(
    readxl::read_excel(params$proteomics_xlsx, sheet = params$proteomics_sheet, col_types = "text"),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(tbl) || !all(c(params$proteomics_gene_column, logfc_col, fdr_col) %in% colnames(tbl)))
    return(NULL)
  tbl %>%
    transmute(gene_id    = trimws(as.character(.data[[params$proteomics_gene_column]])),
              prot_fdr   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[fdr_col]])),
              prot_logfc = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.data[[logfc_col]]))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(gene_id), gene_id != "", !is.na(prot_fdr), !is.na(prot_logfc),
           prot_fdr <= params$proteomics_fdr_threshold,
           abs(prot_logfc) > params$proteomics_lfc_threshold) %>%
    arrange(prot_fdr, dplyr::desc(abs(prot_logfc))) %>%
    distinct(gene_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    transmute(gene_id, prot_direction = ifelse(prot_logfc > 0, "Up", "Down"))
}

# RNA volcano restricted to genes that are also proteomics-significant - same
# construction as the pipeline's own volcano_proteomic.pdf, redrawn here in the
# report's own style. RNA-significant genes are coloured by side as in
# volcano() (green left, pink right); their shape says whether RNA and protein
# move the same way.
proteomic_volcano <- function(res, title, num, den, prot_sig) {
  res <- res %>% filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    mutate(rna_significant = padj < params$padj & abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc,
           rna_direction = ifelse(log2FoldChange > 0, "Up", "Down"))
  df <- res %>% inner_join(prot_sig, by = "gene_id") %>%
    mutate(side = ifelse(rna_direction == "Up", "up", "down"),
           agreement = ifelse(rna_direction == prot_direction,
                              "RNA and protein agree", "RNA and protein disagree"),
           label = ifelse(rna_significant, gene_id, NA_character_))
  if (!nrow(df)) return(invisible(NULL))
  ggplot(df, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj))) +
    geom_point(data = filter(df, !rna_significant), shape = 21, size = 1.4, stroke = 0.3,
               fill = VOLC_COL[["ns"]], colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(data = filter(df, rna_significant), aes(fill = side, shape = agreement),
               size = 2.2, stroke = 0.3, colour = "grey20") +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, colour = "grey15",
                             max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = VOLC_COL, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("RNA and protein agree" = 21,
                                  "RNA and protein disagree" = 24), drop = FALSE) +
    guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey60", size = 2.5))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-params$lfc, params$lfc), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(params$padj), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = sprintf(
        paste0("Proteomics-significant genes only (FDR <= %s, |log2FC| > %s)\n",
               "RIGHT, log2FC > 0: higher in %s   |   LEFT, log2FC < 0: higher in %s\n",
               "RNA-significant genes coloured by side; shape = RNA/protein agreement"),
        params$proteomics_fdr_threshold, params$proteomics_lfc_threshold, num, den),
      x = sprintf("log2FC  (%s / %s)   —   positive = higher in %s", num, den, num),
      y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p"), shape = NULL) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(lineheight = 1.2, size = 8.5), legend.position = "bottom")
}

# The full RNA volcano (volcano()'s own dots, every gene, and the same top-N
# gene labels), with proteomics-significant genes redrawn as stars on top: blue
# if also RNA-significant, black otherwise. The blue stars get their own label
# (a gene already starred blue is skipped from the general top-N labels below,
# so it is never labelled twice).
volcano_with_proteomic <- function(res, title, num, den, prot_sig,
                                   label_top = params$volcano_label_top) {
  res <- res %>% filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
    mutate(sig = padj < params$padj & abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc)
  n <- c(up = sum(res$sig & res$log2FoldChange > 0),
         down = sum(res$sig & res$log2FoldChange < 0))
  stars <- res %>% inner_join(prot_sig, by = "gene_id")
  stars_sig    <- stars %>% filter(sig)
  stars_nonsig <- stars %>% filter(!sig)
  p <- ggplot(res, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj))) +
    volcano_dots(res) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-params$lfc, params$lfc), linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(params$padj), linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = sprintf(
        paste0("%s significant (padj < %s, |log2FC| >= %s)\n",
               "RIGHT, log2FC > 0: %s genes HIGHER in %s   |   ",
               "LEFT, log2FC < 0: %s genes HIGHER in %s\n",
               "★ proteomics-significant (FDR <= %s, |log2FC| > %s): ",
               "blue = also RNA-significant, black = not"),
        format(sum(res$sig), big.mark = ","), params$padj, params$lfc,
        format(n["up"], big.mark = ","), num,
        format(n["down"], big.mark = ","), den,
        params$proteomics_fdr_threshold, params$proteomics_lfc_threshold),
      x = sprintf("log2FC  (%s / %s)   —   positive = higher in %s", num, den, num),
      y = expression(-log[10] ~ "adjusted p")) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(lineheight = 1.2, size = 8.5))
  # Same top-N labelling as volcano(): ranked by -log10(padj) x |log2FC|.
  # Genes already labelled blue below are skipped here to avoid a duplicate.
  star_sig_ids <- tolower(stars_sig$gene_id)
  if (label_top > 0) {
    lbl <- res %>% filter(sig, !tolower(gene_id) %in% star_sig_ids) %>%
      mutate(score = -log10(padj) * abs(log2FoldChange)) %>%
      slice_max(score, n = label_top, with_ties = FALSE)
    if (nrow(lbl)) {
      p <- p + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = lbl, aes(label = gene_id), colour = "grey20", size = 2.4,
        max.overlaps = 30, segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey50",
        show.legend = FALSE)
    }
  }
  if (nrow(stars_nonsig)) {
    p <- p + geom_point(data = stars_nonsig, shape = 8, size = 2, colour = "black")
  }
  if (nrow(stars_sig)) {
    # bg.color/bg.r draw a white halo behind the text, which keeps a label
    # readable where it crosses the coloured significant dots.
    p <- p + geom_point(data = stars_sig, shape = 8, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.8,
                        colour = HL_COL) +
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = stars_sig, aes(label = gene_id), colour = "grey10",
        fontface = "bold", size = 2.8, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.4,
        segment.colour = HL_COL, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE,
        bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.15)
  }
  p
}
```

# Experimental design

```{r design}
data.frame(
  Group = c("TP53", "E6", "EmptyVector", "ATRX_FL", "ATRX_IFF"),
  Description = c("TP53 KO", "TP53 KO + ATRX KO",
                  "E6 + empty EGFP/mCherry vector",
                  "E6 + vector w/ ATRX full length (rescue)",
                  "E6 + vector w/ ATRX in-frame fusion (semi-rescue)"),
  `Parental clone` = c("TP53", "E6", "E6", "E6", "E6"),
  Vector = c("none", "none", "empty", "ATRX-FL", "ATRX-IFF"),
  n = c(3, 3, 3, 3, 3), check.names = FALSE
) %>% kable()
```

> Every group is a single clone, and each
> construct is a single transduced pool. The TP53 line and the E6 lineage differ
> by clonal background as well as by ATRX genotype, and those two cannot be
> separated in this design. Comparisons **within** the E6 lineage
> (`ATRX_FL` / `ATRX_IFF` / `EmptyVector`) are internally controlled and are the
> ones to trust; comparisons **against TP53** carry the clonal difference and are
> shown for completeness only.

---

# Quality control

## Library-level metrics

```{r qc-lib, fig.height = 6}
if (is.null(qc)) missing_note("design_qc", "design_qc_summary.csv") else {
  # "Reads assigned" alone has no denominator - a low bar could mean a small
  # library or a poor assignment rate. featureCounts' own total is recovered
  # from assigned_reads and pct_assigned so both are on the page.
  d <- qc %>% mutate(condition = cond_factor(condition),
                     sample = factor(sample, levels = meta$sample),
                     total_reads = if ("pct_assigned" %in% names(qc))
                       assigned_reads / (pct_assigned / 100) else NA_real_)
  lvls <- c("Total reads (featureCounts input)", "Reads assigned to genes",
            "% reads assigned", "Genes detected")
  print(
    d %>% select(sample, condition, total_reads, assigned_reads,
                 pct_assigned, genes_detected) %>%
      pivot_longer(c(total_reads, assigned_reads, pct_assigned, genes_detected)) %>%
      mutate(name = recode(name,
                           total_reads = "Total reads (featureCounts input)",
                           assigned_reads = "Reads assigned to genes",
                           pct_assigned = "% reads assigned",
                           genes_detected = "Genes detected"),
             name = factor(name, levels = lvls)) %>%
      filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
      ggplot(aes(sample, value, fill = condition)) +
      geom_col() +
      facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = PAL) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x)
        format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Condition") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  )
}
```

> No group-linked shift in either depth, complexity or assignment rate. The libraries
> are comparable.

## ATRX and vector markers

ATRX_wt is the wild-type version, it includes introns, 3'UTR and 5'UTR. ATRX_FL
(7482 bp) and ATRX_IFF (3993 bp) include a Twin-Strep-tag and 10xHis tag, and are
cDNAs (no 3'/5'UTR, no introns).

ATRX_wt, ATRX_FL and ATRX_IFF only account for uniquely mappable reads: reads that
are unambiguously assigned to one of the 3 possible references. That is:

- Reads mapping to either ATRX 3'/5'UTR and reads overlapping exons and introns
  (reads only spanning introns are not counted) are reported as `ATRX_wt`.
- Read pairs with one mate on the Twin-Strep/10His tag and the other past the
  FL/IFF divergence point (nt 250) are reported as `ATRX_FL`.
- Read pairs spanning the fusion breakpoint are reported as `ATRX_IFF`.

Two further rows are counted from the same alignments but keep the multi-mapping
reads:

- `ATRX_Total`: all reads from any ATRX source — wild-type, FL and IFF pooled, tag
  included. Much higher than the sum of the three rows above, which discard
  multimapped reads. Counts scale with transcript length, so the shorter IFF
  construct is under-represented 1.87-fold.
- `Tag`: reads on the Twin-Strep/10His tag only. Most reliable `ATRX_IFF` vs
  `ATRX_FL` expression comparison.

```{r qc-markers, fig.height = 11}
mk <- gene_long(grab("design_qc", "marker_expression.csv"), meta)
if (is.null(mk)) missing_note("design_qc", "marker_expression.csv") else {
  # Keep the CSV's row order (ATRX_Total and Tag first) instead of letting
  # ggplot sort the facets alphabetically, and match the pipeline's ATRX_wt
  # label. The CSV itself keeps the real feature IDs.
  relabel <- function(x) ifelse(x == "ATRX", "ATRX_wt", x)
  mk$gene_id <- factor(relabel(mk$gene_id), levels = relabel(unique(mk$gene_id)))
  print(
    ggplot(mk, aes(sample, value, fill = condition)) +
      geom_col() +
      facet_wrap(~ gene_id, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = PAL) +
      labs(title = "Reporter and transgene expression",
           x = NULL, y = "normalised count", fill = "Condition") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  )
}
```

```{r qc-atrx-table}
mk2 <- grab("design_qc", "marker_expression.csv")
if (!is.null(mk2) && "ATRX" %in% mk2$gene_id && !is.null(meta)) {
  gene_long(mk2, meta) %>% filter(gene_id == "ATRX") %>%
    group_by(condition) %>%
    summarise(mean = round(mean(value)), min = round(min(value)),
              max = round(max(value)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(`% of TP53` = round(100 * mean / mean[condition == "TP53"]),
           `fold spread` = sprintf("%.1fx", max / pmax(min, 1))) %>%
    kable(caption = "ATRX_wt (endogenous locus), normalised counts")
}
```

> `EGFP`/`mCherry` are present only in the transduced groups, although with large
> variations; each ATRX construct is detected only in its own group. `E6` seems to
> have a reduced expression compared to `TP53`, possibly because the CRISPR
> modification in ATRX introduced a premature stop codon leading to
> nonsense-mediated decay. `ATRX_wt` and `ATRX_Total` show very similar profiles,
> which is expected for `TP53` and `E6`; however for `ATRX_FL` and `ATRX_IFF` one
> would expect a bump in expression due to multimapped construct reads. Via the
> `Tag` expression, we see that `ATRX_IFF` is much more expressed than `ATRX_FL`.

## Sample–sample correlation

```{r qc-cor, fig.height = 6}
cm <- grab("design_qc", "sample_correlation.csv")
if (is.null(cm)) missing_note("design_qc", "sample_correlation.csv") else {
  m <- as.matrix(cm[, -1]); rownames(m) <- cm$sample
  ord <- meta$sample[meta$sample %in% rownames(m)]
  m <- m[ord, ord]
  print(
    as.data.frame(as.table(m)) %>%
      setNames(c("x", "y", "rho")) %>%
      mutate(x = factor(x, ord), y = factor(y, rev(ord))) %>%
      ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = rho)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
      scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166AC") +
      coord_fixed() +
      labs(title = "Spearman correlation (VST)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            panel.grid = element_blank())
  )
}
```

> Replicates should form tight blocks on the diagonal. There is a very strong clonal effect between TP53 and E6 samples, that almost obfuscate the replicates correlation.

---

# Global structure (PCA)

```{r pca, fig.height = 5, results = "asis"}
# One view only: the E6-derived PCA has its own section at the end of the report.
# The ATRX features are removed here as well as the reporters - ATRX is the
# variable under study, so leaving it in makes the PCA partly re-plot the design
# rather than its downstream consequences.
pca_views <- list(
  c("all", "no_vector_no_transgene",
    "All samples, reporter and ATRX features removed")
)
for (v in pca_views) {
  co <- grab("pca", v[1], paste0(v[2], "_coords.csv"))
  ve <- grab("pca", v[1], paste0(v[2], "_variance_explained.csv"))
  cat("\n\n##", v[3], "\n\n")
  if (is.null(co)) { missing_note("pca", v[1], paste0(v[2], "_coords.csv")); next }
  pv <- if (!is.null(ve)) setNames(ve$percent_variance, ve$PC) else c(PC1 = NA, PC2 = NA)
  p <- co %>% mutate(condition = cond_factor(condition)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = condition, label = sample)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE, max.overlaps = 20) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL) +
    labs(title = v[3],
         x = sprintf("PC1: %.1f%% variance", pv[["PC1"]]),
         y = sprintf("PC2: %.1f%% variance", pv[["PC2"]]),
         colour = "Condition")
  print(p)
}
```

> PC1 (78%) of the full PCA separates TP53 from everything E6-derived with :
> heavy clonal background, as seen with the sample-sample variance, confounded with the ATRX genotype and not correctable.

---

# How TP53 differs from the E6 lineage

Before narrowing to the E6 samples only, this is the size of the difference we are
setting aside. `TP53` is a different clone from everything E6-derived, and that
difference is confounded with the ATRX genotype.

```{r tp53-vs-e6, fig.height = 5}
r_tp53 <- de_results("deseq2", "E6_vs_TP53", "results.csv")
if (is.null(r_tp53)) missing_note("deseq2", "E6_vs_TP53", "results.csv") else {
  print(volcano(r_tp53, "E6_vs_TP53", num = "E6", den = "TP53"))
}
```

```{r tp53-scale, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(r_tp53)) {
  n <- de_counts(r_tp53)
  cat(sprintf(paste("\n> **%s genes** change between TP53 and E6 at padj < %s and",
                    "|log2FC| >= %s (%s up in E6, %s down) - roughly %.0f%% of the",
                    "genes tested. That is the clone plus the ATRX knockout",
                    "together, and it dwarfs everything that follows.\n\n"),
              format(sum(n), big.mark = ","), params$padj, params$lfc,
              format(n["up"], big.mark = ","), format(n["down"], big.mark = ","),
              100 * sum(n) / sum(!is.na(r_tp53$padj))))
}
```

```{r tp53-top}
if (!is.null(r_tp53)) kable(top_genes(r_tp53), caption = "E6_vs_TP53: top genes")
```

> With 18% of the genes teste being significantly differently expressed between TP53 and E6, 
> we can see that either the clonal drift or the ATRX knockout led to huge shifts in expression.
> Our current set up does not enable us to separate the two, clonal background and ATRX status vary together and are perfectly confounded


## Differential expression across contrasts

Gene counts only. The per-contrast volcanoes are in the pipeline output under
`deseq2/{contrast}/`; what matters here is the relative size of each effect.

`r sprintf("The vector and transgene features (%s) are excluded from every differential-expression figure and table in this report. They are constructs rather than biology, and in any contrast crossing a construct boundary they would otherwise top the list.", paste(params$exclude_genes, collapse = ", "))`

```{r de-tally}
# Self-contained: reads each contrast's results and counts, without drawing
# anything. The headline ATRX_FL vs ATRX_IFF comparison is included so the
# cleanest contrast in the design can be sized against the rest.
tally_contrasts <- c(
  params$headline_contrast,
  "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector",
  "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector",
  "EmptyVector_vs_E6",
  "E6_vs_TP53",
  "ATRX_FL_vs_TP53",
  "ATRX_IFF_vs_TP53"
)
tally <- list()
for (cn in tally_contrasts) {
  r <- de_results("deseq2", cn, "results.csv")
  if (!is.null(r)) tally[[cn]] <- de_counts(r)
}
if (length(tally)) {
  do.call(rbind, tally) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("contrast") %>%
    mutate(total = up + down) %>%
    kable(caption = sprintf("Genes with padj < %s and |log2FC| >= %s",
                            params$padj, params$lfc))
} else {
  missing_note("deseq2", "*", "results.csv")
}
```

---

# Rescue assessment

Whether the rescue worked is not answerable by asking if `ATRX_FL` clusters
with `TP53` — different clone, different transduction status. Instead: does the
intervention push the knockout-responsive genes back the other way? Both
contrasts used here sit inside a single genetic background, so the clonal
difference never enters.

## Signature reversal

```{r rescue-stats}
srs <- list.files(file.path(OUT, "signature_reversal"), pattern = "reversal_stats.csv",
                  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
if (!length(srs)) missing_note("signature_reversal", "*", "reversal_stats.csv") else {
  # bind_rows, not rbind: stats files written by different versions of the script
  # can have different column sets, and rbind would abort the whole render.
  tab <- bind_rows(lapply(srs, read.csv)) %>%
    select(any_of(c("comparison", "n_signature_genes", "pct_reversed",
                    "null_pct_reversed", "excess_over_null", "perm_p",
                    "spearman_rho", "interpretable")))
  if ("excess_over_null" %in% names(tab)) tab <- arrange(tab, desc(excess_over_null))
  stale <- setdiff(c("null_pct_reversed", "excess_over_null", "perm_p"), names(tab))
  if (length(stale)) {
    cat("\n> **Note:** some `reversal_stats.csv` files predate the permutation",
        "null and lack", paste0("`", stale, "`", collapse = ", "),
        "- re-run those comparisons.\n\n")
  }
  kable(tab, caption = paste("Reversal of the knockout signature. Read the excess",
                             "over the permutation null, not the raw percentage."))
}
```

```{r rescue-scatter, fig.height = 6, results = "asis"}
# EDIT: which comparison to draw in full. The negative control pairs the vector-
# transduction signature (E6 vs EmptyVector) against the FL-vs-IFF difference -
# two groups that share no sample with the signature and have no mechanistic
# reason to reverse it. It calibrates the two rescue scores above: if it scores
# near the permutation null, the FL/IFF reversal is ATRX-specific; if it scores
# like ATRX_FL does, the metric is picking up generic structure instead.
for (nm in c("ATRX_FL_reverses_KO_signature_lfc1",
             "ATRX_IFF_reverses_KO_signature_lfc1",
             "NEGATIVE_CONTROL_vector_signature_vs_FL_IFF")) {
  g <- grab("signature_reversal", nm, "reversal_genes.csv")
  heading <- if (nm == "NEGATIVE_CONTROL_vector_signature_vs_FL_IFF")
    paste(nm, "(negative control)") else nm
  cat("\n\n###", heading, "\n\n")
  if (is.null(g)) { missing_note("signature_reversal", nm, "reversal_genes.csv"); next }
  # Report-only: drop the vector/transgene features still present (ATRX; see
  # exclude_genes above for why EGFP/mCherry/ATRX_FL/ATRX_IFF are not listed
  # here), same as every DE table and volcano above (de_results()).
  g <- g[!tolower(g$gene_id) %in% tolower(params$exclude_genes), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(g)) { cat("\n> No genes left after excluding vector/transgene features.\n\n"); next }
  lim <- max(abs(c(g$lfc_sig, g$lfc_resp)), na.rm = TRUE)
  st  <- grab("signature_reversal", nm, "reversal_stats.csv")
  # Stats go inside the panel: a long subtitle is silently clipped once the
  # figure is embedded or scaled, and these numbers are the point of the plot.
  box <- if (!is.null(st)) paste(
    sprintf("slope     %+.2f", st$tls_slope[1]),
    sprintf("R2        %.3f", if ("r_squared" %in% names(st))
              st$r_squared[1] else st$pearson_r[1]^2),
    sprintf("rho       %+.2f", st$spearman_rho[1]),
    sprintf("reversed  %.0f%% (null %.0f%%)", st$pct_reversed[1],
            st$null_pct_reversed[1]),
    sprintf("perm p    %s", format(signif(st$perm_p[1], 2))), sep = "\n") else NULL
  is_control <- nm == "NEGATIVE_CONTROL_vector_signature_vs_FL_IFF"
  # Name the actual contrast on each axis, e.g. "E6 / TP53", not a generic
  # "the damage" - matching the pipeline's own reversal_scatter.pdf. Read from
  # reversal_stats.csv (signature_contrast / response_contrast) rather than
  # hardcoding, since that is the one place the exact label is guaranteed to
  # match what the stats box above was computed from.
  sig_label  <- if (!is.null(st) && "signature_contrast" %in% names(st))
    st$signature_contrast[1] else "signature"
  resp_label <- if (!is.null(st) && "response_contrast" %in% names(st))
    st$response_contrast[1] else "response"
  p <- ggplot(g, aes(lfc_sig, lfc_resp)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = lim, ymin = -lim, ymax = 0,
             fill = "#4DAF4A", alpha = .07) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -lim, xmax = 0, ymin = 0, ymax = lim,
             fill = "#4DAF4A", alpha = .07) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_abline(slope = -1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
    geom_point(size = 1, alpha = .5, colour = "#2166AC") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-lim, lim), ylim = c(-lim, lim)) +
    labs(title = heading,
         subtitle = paste0("shaded = reversal | dashed = complete reversal (slope -1)\n",
                           "red = fitted slope (total least squares)"),
         x = sprintf("log2FC  %s%s", sig_label,
                     if (is_control) "" else "   (the perturbation)"),
         y = sprintf("log2FC  %s%s", resp_label,
                     if (is_control) "" else "   (the intervention)"))
  # The fitted slope is the statistic being reported, so draw it rather than
  # leaving the reader to infer it from the box.
  if (!is.null(st) && "tls_slope" %in% names(st) && is.finite(st$tls_slope[1])) {
    p <- p + geom_abline(slope = st$tls_slope[1], intercept = 0,
                         colour = "#E41A1C", linewidth = .8)
  }
  if (!is.null(box)) {
    p <- p + annotate("label", x = lim, y = lim, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, label = box,
                      size = 2.9, family = "mono", lineheight = 1.15,
                      fill = grDevices::adjustcolor("white", alpha.f = .88),
                      label.size = .25, colour = "grey15")
  }
  print(p)
}
```

> If a gene was pushed up by the knockout it should be pushed back down when reintroducing ATRX: points in the shaded
> quadrants, along the dashed line. Slope −1 is a complete rescue, 0 is no
> response. We see a slightly higher recovery in `ATRX_FL` compared to `ATRX_IFF`,
> however, both are very close to zero. Furthermore, using E6/EmptyVector vs FL/IFF as a control,
> we see that we obtain a steeper slope with a better $R^2$, while there should be no rescue there. 
> Therefore, we can conclude that there is no significant proof of rescue when introducing ATRX_FL.
> Any rescue effect could possibly be obfuscated by the large difference observed between the TP53 and E6 clones.

# The E6 lineage alone

With `TP53` excluded, every remaining group shares one clone and one
transduction step. Differences here are attributable to the construct — the two
effects we could not separate above are now held constant by design rather than
corrected for.

### The two constructs against each other

```{r e6-three-fl-iff-rna, fig.height = 4.5, results = "asis"}
r_fl_iff <- de_results("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL", "results.csv")
if (is.null(r_fl_iff)) {
  missing_note("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL", "results.csv")
} else {
  trio_tally[["ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL"]] <- de_counts(r_fl_iff)
  print(volcano(r_fl_iff, "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL", num = "ATRX_IFF", den = "ATRX_FL"))
  cat("\n\n")
  print(kable(top_genes(r_fl_iff, n = 8)))
}
```

> HOXB, PAX6 and SIM2 are overexpressed in `ATRX_IFF` compared to `ATRX_FL`. 
> They are canonical targets of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).
> `ATRX_IFF` lacks its EZH2 (PRC2 member) interacting domain. Hypothesis: it fails recruiting PRC2 at the HOXB locus,
> leading to a de-repression of those genes.


```{r e6-three-fl-iff-prot, fig.height = 4.5, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(r_fl_iff)) {
  prot_sig <- load_proteomics_sig()
  if (is.null(prot_sig)) {
    cat("\n> **Not available.** Proteomics overlay skipped: `params$proteomics_xlsx`",
        "was not found, or is missing the expected sheet/columns for comparison",
        paste0("`", params$proteomics_comparison, "`.\n\n"))
  } else {
    cat("\n\n**Proteomics concordance (RNA vs LC-MS/MS protein), same contrast:**\n\n")
    print(proteomic_volcano(r_fl_iff, "Proteomics-filtered: ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL",
                            num = "ATRX_IFF", den = "ATRX_FL", prot_sig))
  }
}
```

> The volcano plot above is the same as the previous one, only filtered for genes that are significant hits in the proteomics analysis.
> Most proteomic hits are not significantly overexpressed on the transcriptomic level. When they are overexpressed, hits are concording:
> a protein that interacted more with `ATRX_IFF` than `ATRX_FL` has its gene overexpressed in `ATRX_IFF`.
> RMM2 is an E2F1 target, CDK6 is an upstream activator of E2F (via RB phosphorylation). TFRC is a MYC target.
> IGF2BP1 is one of the top upregulated gene in `ATRX_IFF` and is a known stabilizator for E2F/MYC mRNAs (also binds to HOXB).

# Pathway enrichment (GSEA)

Each plot shows the significant pathways (`padj < 0.05`). Under it, a
scrollable table lists the same pathways in the same order, with their
**leading-edge genes**: the pathway genes ranked before the enrichment score
peaks, i.e. the ones driving the enrichment — not every gene in the pathway,
and not necessarily individually significant.

```{r gsea, results = "asis"}
# Significant pathways only (padj < params$padj), the top N by |NES| per side.
gsea_dot <- function(df, title, top = 12) {
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < params$padj) %>% arrange(desc(abs(NES)))
  df <- bind_rows(head(filter(df, NES > 0), top), head(filter(df, NES < 0), top))
  if (!nrow(df)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nNo pathway with padj < %s.\n\n", params$padj))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  num <- df$numerator[1]; den <- df$denominator[1]
  up   <- sprintf("NES > 0: pathway genes HIGHER in %s", num)
  down <- sprintf("NES < 0: pathway genes HIGHER in %s", den)
  df <- df %>% mutate(
    pathway = gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway),
    pathway = factor(pathway, levels = pathway[order(df$NES)]),
    side = factor(ifelse(NES > 0, up, down), levels = c(up, down)))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(NES, pathway, colour = padj, size = size)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    # Strip labels wrapped onto two lines: on one, the strip takes more
    # width than the dots.
    facet_grid(side ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
               labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 22)) +
    scale_colour_padj() +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = sprintf("enrichment of the %s / %s ranking", num, den),
         y = NULL, colour = "padj", size = "Set size") +
    theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8))
  show_enrich(p, df$pathway, nrow(df) + 2)
  gsea_table(df)
}
# EDIT: which contrasts to show enrichment for.
for (cn in c("ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL", "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector",
             "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector")) {
  g <- grab("gsea", cn, "H_results.csv")
  cat("\n\n##", cn, "\n\n")
  if (is.null(g)) { missing_note("gsea", cn, "H_results.csv"); next }
  gsea_dot(g, paste("Hallmark:", cn))
}
```

> Hallmark proliferation sets (E2F, G2M, MYC) are enriched in `ATRX_IFF` compared to `ATRX_FL`, and
> the inflammatory/interferon sets are enriched in `ATRX_FL`.

## Pathway categories

After concertation with Magdalena Rados, the pathway categories below were selected:

- Replication and repair,
- Chromosome
- Cell growth and death
- Nervous system
- Development and regeneration

Corresponding signatures were selected in the KEGG database, and matched in the GO database:

- **KEGG**: signatures drawn from the live KEGG definitions
- **GO**: Each group is a **keyword search** designed to match the selected KEGG categories. The exact regular expression pattern used for each category is printed under its panel below.


```{r pathway-categories, fig.height = 4.5, results = "asis"}
CATEGORY_LABELS <- c(replication_and_repair       = "Replication and repair",
                      chromosome                   = "Chromosome",
                      cell_growth_and_death        = "Cell growth and death",
                      nervous_system               = "Nervous system",
                      development_and_regeneration = "Development and regeneration")

# The GO include regexes actually used for each category
# (workflow/resources/go_categories.tsv), copied here so the reasoning behind
# each GO panel sits right next to it instead of only living in the pipeline.
# All five have no exclude pattern ("-" in the TSV).
GO_KEYWORDS <- c(
  replication_and_repair =
    "DNA_REPLICATION|DNA_REPAIR|MISMATCH_REPAIR|EXCISION_REPAIR|DOUBLE_STRAND_BREAK|HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION|END_JOINING|REPLICATION_FORK|TRANSLESION|POSTREPLICATION|DNA_DAMAGE_CHECKPOINT|DNA_INTEGRITY",
  chromosome =
    "CHROMATIN|CHROMOSOM|NUCLEOSOME|HISTONE|HETEROCHROMATIN|EUCHROMATIN|CENTROMER|KINETOCHORE|TELOMER|COHESIN|CONDENSIN|SISTER_CHROMATID|DNA_PACKAGING|POLYCOMB",
  cell_growth_and_death =
    "CELL_CYCLE|MITOTIC|MEIOTIC|MEIOSIS|APOPTOT|APOPTOSIS|NECROPTO|FERROPTO|PYROPTO|CELL_DEATH|SENESCENCE|CELL_PROLIFERATION|GROWTH_ARREST|G1_S_TRANSITION|G2_M_TRANSITION|SPINDLE_CHECKPOINT",
  nervous_system =
    "NEURON|NEURAL|NEURO|SYNAP|AXON|DENDRIT|GLIAL|ASTROCYTE|OLIGODENDROCYTE|NEUROTRANSMITTER|NERVE|FOREBRAIN|HINDBRAIN|MIDBRAIN|LONG_TERM_POTENTIATION|LONG_TERM_SYNAPTIC",
  development_and_regeneration =
    "DEVELOPMENT|MORPHOGENESIS|REGENERATION|PATTERN_SPECIFICATION|ORGANOGENESIS|CELL_FATE|AXIS_SPECIFICATION|STEM_CELL_DIFFERENTIATION|TISSUE_REMODELING"
)
# Matches GSEA.go_categories_top_n in config_epicode.yaml.
GO_TOP_N <- 25

# Significant pathways only (padj < params$padj).
cat_dot <- function(df, title) {
  if (is.null(df)) return(invisible(NULL))
  df <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & df$padj < params$padj, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(df)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nNo pathway with padj < %s.\n\n", params$padj))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  df$pathway <- factor(df$pathway, levels = df$pathway[order(df$NES)])
  sz <- range(df$size, na.rm = TRUE)
  brk <- if (sz[1] == sz[2]) sz[1] else unique(round(c(sz[1], mean(sz), sz[2])))
  # Spell the direction out the same way the Hallmark dotplot above does.
  num <- if ("numerator" %in% names(df)) df$numerator[1] else ""
  den <- if ("denominator" %in% names(df)) df$denominator[1] else ""
  sub <- if (nzchar(num) && nzchar(den))
    sprintf("NES > 0: pathway genes HIGHER in %s   |   NES < 0: pathway genes HIGHER in %s",
            num, den) else NULL
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(NES, pathway)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_point(aes(size = size, colour = padj)) +
    scale_colour_padj() +
    scale_size_continuous(limits = sz, breaks = brk, range = c(2, 8)) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = sub, y = NULL, size = "Set size") +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey30"))
  show_enrich(p, df$pathway, nrow(df))
  gsea_table(df)
}

# EDIT: which contrast to show category panels for. Headline contrast only.
cn <- "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL"
for (slug in names(CATEGORY_LABELS)) {
  label <- CATEGORY_LABELS[[slug]]
  cat("\n\n###", label, "\n\n")

  cat("\n\n**KEGG** — significant pathways in the category\n\n")
  gk <- grab("gsea", cn, "kegg", paste0(slug, "_results.csv"))
  if (is.null(gk)) {
    missing_note("gsea", cn, "kegg", paste0(slug, "_results.csv"))
  } else {
    cat_dot(gk, paste("KEGG:", label))
  }
  cat("\n\n")

  cat("\n\n**GO** — keyword match on term names\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("\n> include: `%s`\n\n", GO_KEYWORDS[[slug]]))
  gg <- grab("gsea", cn, "go", paste0(slug, "_results.csv"))
  if (is.null(gg)) {
    missing_note("gsea", cn, "go", paste0(slug, "_results.csv"))
  } else {
    gg <- gg[!is.na(gg$padj) & gg$padj < params$padj, , drop = FALSE]
    n_matched <- nrow(gg)
    gg <- gg[order(gg$padj, -abs(gg$NES)), , drop = FALSE]
    if (n_matched > GO_TOP_N) {
      cat(sprintf(
        "\n> top %d of %d significant terms by padj; all matches are in `gsea/%s/go/%s_results.csv`\n\n",
        GO_TOP_N, n_matched, cn, slug))
      gg <- gg[seq_len(GO_TOP_N), , drop = FALSE]
    }
    gg$pathway <- gsub("^GOBP_", "", gg$pathway)
    cat_dot(gg, paste("GO:", label))
  }
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Shared by ATRX_FL and ATRX_IFF

What do the two constructs change the same way, relative to their common
control? Genes significant (`padj < 0.05`, `|log2FC| >= 1`) in the same
direction in `ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector` and `ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector`: higher in
both constructs, or higher in `EmptyVector` in both. The centre of each Venn
diagram is then tested against Hallmark, current KEGG and GO
biological-process gene sets. The centre is a gene set rather than a ranking,
so this is an over-representation test (one-sided hypergeometric, against all
genes tested in both contrasts, BH-adjusted), not GSEA.

## Venn diagrams

```{r shared-venn, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.8, results = "asis"}
# SharedGenes.comparisons entry in config_epicode.yaml (pipeline outputs under
# shared_genes/<name>/).
SHARED_NAME <- "ATRX_FL_and_ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector"
r_fl  <- de_results("deseq2", "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector", "results.csv")
r_iff <- de_results("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector", "results.csv")

# Same calls as the pipeline's SharedGenes rule and every DE table above.
sig_genes <- function(r, sign) r$gene_id[!is.na(r$padj) & r$padj < params$padj &
                                           sign * r$log2FoldChange >= params$lfc]

venn_plot <- function(sets) {
  circle <- function(x0) {
    t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
    data.frame(x = x0 + cos(t), y = sin(t))
  }
  shapes <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sets), function(p) bind_rows(
    cbind(circle(-0.6), set = "ATRX_FL", panel = p),
    cbind(circle(0.6), set = "ATRX_IFF", panel = p))))
  counts <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sets), function(p) {
    a <- sets[[p]]$ATRX_FL; b <- sets[[p]]$ATRX_IFF
    data.frame(panel = p, x = c(-1.1, 0, 1.1), y = 0,
               n = c(length(setdiff(a, b)), length(intersect(a, b)), length(setdiff(b, a))))
  }))
  labels <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sets), function(p) data.frame(
    panel = p, x = c(-0.6, 0.6), y = 1.22, hjust = c(0.7, 0.3),
    lab = sprintf("%s vs EmptyVector\n(%d)", c("ATRX_FL", "ATRX_IFF"),
                  lengths(sets[[p]][c("ATRX_FL", "ATRX_IFF")])))))
  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = shapes, aes(x, y, group = set, fill = set, colour = set),
                 alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(data = counts, aes(x, y, label = n), size = 5, colour = "grey10") +
    geom_text(data = labels, aes(x, y, label = lab, hjust = hjust), vjust = 0,
              size = 3.2, colour = "grey20", lineheight = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ factor(panel, levels = names(sets))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL, guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL, guide = "none") +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.8, 1.8), ylim = c(-1.1, 1.65), clip = "off") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(b = 6)))
}

if (is.null(r_fl) || is.null(r_iff)) {
  if (is.null(r_fl))  missing_note("deseq2", "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector", "results.csv")
  if (is.null(r_iff)) missing_note("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector", "results.csv")
} else {
  sets <- list(
    "Higher in the construct" = list(ATRX_FL = sig_genes(r_fl, 1), ATRX_IFF = sig_genes(r_iff, 1)),
    "Higher in EmptyVector"   = list(ATRX_FL = sig_genes(r_fl, -1), ATRX_IFF = sig_genes(r_iff, -1)))
  print(venn_plot(sets))

  # All shared genes, strongest first (smaller |log2FC| of the two), in a
  # scrollable box.
  shared_table <- function(s, sign, label) {
    g <- intersect(s$ATRX_FL, s$ATRX_IFF)
    if (!length(g)) return(invisible(NULL))
    d <- inner_join(r_fl[r_fl$gene_id %in% g, c("gene_id", "log2FoldChange", "padj")],
                    r_iff[r_iff$gene_id %in% g, c("gene_id", "log2FoldChange", "padj")],
                    by = "gene_id", suffix = c("_FL", "_IFF"))
    d <- d[order(-pmin(sign * d$log2FoldChange_FL, sign * d$log2FoldChange_IFF)), ]
    cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s in both: %d genes**, sorted by the smaller |log2FC| of the two\n\n",
                label, nrow(d)))
    cat('<div style="max-height: 320px; overflow-y: auto; margin-bottom: 1em;">\n')
    print(kable(transmute(d, gene_id,
                          `log2FC FL` = round(log2FoldChange_FL, 2),
                          `log2FC IFF` = round(log2FoldChange_IFF, 2),
                          `padj FL` = fmt_p(padj_FL),
                          `padj IFF` = fmt_p(padj_IFF)),
                format = "html", row.names = FALSE,
                table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed"'))
    cat("\n</div>\n\n")
  }
  shared_table(sets[[1]], 1, "Higher in the construct")
  shared_table(sets[[2]], -1, "Higher in EmptyVector")
}
```

## Enrichment of the shared genes

**Exploratory.** With only a few dozen shared genes, few or no gene sets
survive multiple-testing correction, so the plots show gene sets with a
**nominal** `p < 0.05` (at most the top 20 by `p`), coloured by that nominal
`p`. Filled points also pass BH FDR `< 0.05` (within each direction and
collection); hollow points pass the nominal threshold only and are leads to
follow up, not results. Fold enrichment is the observed overlap over the
overlap expected by chance;
`shared_genes/ATRX_FL_and_ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector/ora_*.csv` keeps every set
tested, with both `pvalue` and `padj`.

```{r shared-ora, fig.height = 4.5, results = "asis"}
# Exploratory: nominal p < params$padj (same 0.05 cutoff), top N by p.
# Filled = also BH FDR < cutoff, hollow = nominal only.
ora_dot <- function(df, title, top = 20) {
  cut <- params$padj
  df <- df[!is.na(df$pvalue) & df$pvalue < cut, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(df)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nNo gene set with nominal p < %s.\n\n", cut))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  df <- head(df[order(df$pvalue, -df$fold_enrichment), ], top)
  df$pathway <- gsub("^(HALLMARK|GOBP)_", "", df$pathway)
  df$pathway <- factor(df$pathway, levels = df$pathway[order(df$fold_enrichment)])
  fdr_levels <- c(sprintf("FDR < %s", cut), sprintf("nominal p < %s only", cut))
  df$fdr <- factor(ifelse(df$padj < cut, fdr_levels[1], fdr_levels[2]), levels = fdr_levels)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(fold_enrichment, pathway, colour = pvalue, size = overlap, shape = fdr)) +
    geom_point(stroke = 1.1) +
    scale_colour_padj(name = "nominal p") +
    scale_size_continuous(breaks = int_breaks) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(19, 1), fdr_levels), drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "grey30", size = 3))) +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = sprintf("%d of the %d sets shown pass BH FDR < %s",
                            sum(df$padj < cut), nrow(df), cut),
         x = "fold enrichment (observed / expected overlap)",
         y = NULL, size = "Shared genes in set")
  show_enrich(p, df$pathway, nrow(df))
  df <- df[order(-df$fold_enrichment), , drop = FALSE]
  scroll_table(data.frame(pathway = as.character(df$pathway), `shared genes in set` = df$overlap,
                          `set size` = df$set_size,
                          `fold enrichment` = round(df$fold_enrichment, 2),
                          p = fmt_p(df$pvalue), padj = fmt_p(df$padj),
                          genes = genes_list(df$genes), check.names = FALSE))
}

ORA_COLLECTIONS <- c(H = "Hallmark", KEGG_CURRENT = "KEGG (current)",
                     C5_GO_BP = "GO biological process")
for (dir in c("up", "down")) {
  heading <- if (dir == "up") "Higher in both ATRX constructs" else "Higher in EmptyVector in both"
  short   <- if (dir == "up") "higher in ATRX_FL and ATRX_IFF" else "higher in EmptyVector (vs both)"
  cat("\n\n###", heading, "\n\n")
  for (slug in names(ORA_COLLECTIONS)) {
    f <- sprintf("ora_%s_%s.csv", dir, slug)
    o <- grab("shared_genes", SHARED_NAME, f)
    if (is.null(o)) { missing_note("shared_genes", SHARED_NAME, f); next }
    ora_dot(o, paste0(ORA_COLLECTIONS[[slug]], ": ", short))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

## Shared pathways (test)

The same question at the pathway level, using every gene: the pipeline's GSEA
of `ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector` and of `ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector` (fgsea on the
DESeq2 Wald statistic), compared. A pathway is **shared** when it is
significant (`padj < 0.05`) in both comparisons with the same NES sign. For
each collection: Venn diagrams of the significant pathways per direction, the
NES of every pathway significant in at least one comparison (shared ones
labelled), and a table of the shared pathways with both leading edges.

```{r shared-gsea, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.8, results = "asis"}
GSEA_SHARED <- c(H = "Hallmark", KEGG_CURRENT = "KEGG (current)",
                 C5_GO_BP = "GO biological process")
short_name <- function(x, n = 45) {
  x <- gsub("^(HALLMARK|GOBP|KEGG)_", "", x)
  ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n - 1), "\u2026"), x)
}
for (slug in names(GSEA_SHARED)) {
  cat("\n\n###", GSEA_SHARED[[slug]], "\n\n")
  f <- paste0(slug, "_results.csv")
  fl  <- grab("gsea", "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector", f)
  iff <- grab("gsea", "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector", f)
  if (is.null(fl) || is.null(iff)) {
    if (is.null(fl))  missing_note("gsea", "ATRX_FL_vs_EmptyVector", f)
    if (is.null(iff)) missing_note("gsea", "ATRX_IFF_vs_EmptyVector", f)
    next
  }
  cols <- c("pathway", "NES", "padj", "size", "leadingEdge")
  m <- inner_join(fl[, intersect(cols, names(fl))], iff[, intersect(cols, names(iff))],
                  by = "pathway", suffix = c("_FL", "_IFF"))
  sig_fl  <- !is.na(m$padj_FL)  & m$padj_FL  < params$padj
  sig_iff <- !is.na(m$padj_IFF) & m$padj_IFF < params$padj
  print(venn_plot(list(
    "NES > 0: higher in the construct" =
      list(ATRX_FL = m$pathway[sig_fl & m$NES_FL > 0], ATRX_IFF = m$pathway[sig_iff & m$NES_IFF > 0]),
    "NES < 0: higher in EmptyVector" =
      list(ATRX_FL = m$pathway[sig_fl & m$NES_FL < 0], ATRX_IFF = m$pathway[sig_iff & m$NES_IFF < 0]))))

  m$class <- case_when(
    sig_fl & sig_iff & sign(m$NES_FL) == sign(m$NES_IFF) ~ "shared (same direction)",
    sig_fl & sig_iff ~ "opposite directions",
    sig_fl ~ "ATRX_FL only",
    sig_iff ~ "ATRX_IFF only",
    TRUE ~ "neither")
  d <- m[m$class != "neither", , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nNo pathway with padj < %s in either comparison.\n\n", params$padj))
    next
  }
  shared <- d[d$class == "shared (same direction)", , drop = FALSE]
  # Strongest shared effect first: the smaller |NES| of the two comparisons.
  shared <- shared[order(-pmin(abs(shared$NES_FL), abs(shared$NES_IFF))), , drop = FALSE]
  lab <- head(shared, 15)
  lim <- max(abs(c(d$NES_FL, d$NES_IFF)))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(NES_FL, NES_IFF)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = class), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.85) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = short_name(pathway)), size = 2.5,
                             colour = "grey15", max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0,
                             segment.colour = "grey50", segment.size = 0.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("shared (same direction)" = "grey10",
                                   "ATRX_FL only" = PAL[["ATRX_FL"]],
                                   "ATRX_IFF only" = PAL[["ATRX_IFF"]],
                                   "opposite directions" = "grey70"), name = NULL) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(-lim, lim), ylim = c(-lim, lim)) +
    labs(title = paste0(GSEA_SHARED[[slug]], ": NES in both comparisons"),
         subtitle = sprintf("pathways with padj < %s in at least one; %d shared, %d labelled",
                            params$padj, nrow(shared), nrow(lab)),
         x = "NES  ATRX_FL vs EmptyVector", y = "NES  ATRX_IFF vs EmptyVector")
  show_plot(p, width = 7.5, height = 6.2)

  if (!nrow(shared)) {
    cat("\nNo shared pathway.\n\n")
    next
  }
  shared <- shared[order(shared$NES_FL < 0), , drop = FALSE]  # NES > 0 first, order kept
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**Shared pathways: %d**\n\n", nrow(shared)))
  scroll_table(data.frame(
    pathway = shared$pathway,
    direction = ifelse(shared$NES_FL > 0, "higher in the construct", "higher in EmptyVector"),
    `NES FL` = round(shared$NES_FL, 2), `padj FL` = fmt_p(shared$padj_FL),
    `NES IFF` = round(shared$NES_IFF, 2), `padj IFF` = fmt_p(shared$padj_IFF),
    `leading edge FL` = genes_list(shared$leadingEdge_FL),
    `leading edge IFF` = genes_list(shared$leadingEdge_IFF), check.names = FALSE),
    max_height = 400)
}
```
